written.myAnswer: The stomach’s epithelial tissue secretes mucus to protect its lining and gastric juice, including hydrochloric acid and pepsinogen, to help digest proteins.
The smooth muscle layers contract and relax to churn and mix food with gastric juice.
A tissue is a group of similar cells working together to perform a specific function. An organ consists of different tissues working together to perform specific functions.

The stomach has epithelial tissue, connective tissue, smooth muscle, and an outer covering. The epithelium secretes mucus and gastric juice; connective tissue supports the stomach and contains blood vessels, nerves, and lymphatics; smooth muscle mixes food with gastric juice; and the outer layer helps cover and support the stomach.
Organ systems are groups of organs that work together to perform functions. The different systems cooperate to maintain and coordinate the functions of the human body.

Organ systems depend on one another to carry out body functions. If one system fails, others may be affected—for example, respiratory failure can reduce oxygen entering the blood and therefore reduce oxygen delivery to body cells.
